cues.en: Hello fellows, I am rumaging through my HP instrument collection and I put some items in suitcases and as you can see the suitcases have a NASA sticker on them and the occasion is momentous. I am going to rejoin Carl and Ken and some others in Houston because we have been asked to help with the restoration of the Apollo guidance computer.
cues.zh: 大家好，我正在翻找我收藏的 HP 仪器，并把一些装进了箱子里，如大家所见，箱子上贴着 NASA 的贴纸，这次的场合非同小可。我正准备去休斯敦和 Carl、Ken 还有其他人汇合，因为有人邀请我们协助修复阿波罗制导计算机（Apollo guidance computer）。

cues.en: For those that don't know, the Apollo guidance computer is this 1960 famed computer that was aboard the Apollo command module and the LEM and guided the spaceship all the way from Earth to landing on the moon. So you can imagine that when we were asked to help, we said yes pretty quickly and started to pack right away. That looks promising.
cues.zh: 可能有人还不了解，阿波罗制导计算机是 1960 年代著名的计算机，曾搭载在阿波罗指令舱和登月舱上，一路指引飞船从地球飞往月球并着陆。所以你们可以想象，当收到协助邀请时，我们立刻就答应了，马上开始打包行李。看起来进展不错。

cues.en: Sorry guys, I have camera in hand. Hi there, welcome Jimmy Long. Nice to meet you. I'm Tim. Tim, nice to meet you. Hey Mike. Hey. Well, you have gloves. And here's the beast. Okay, we'll do the correct introduction later on. I have the lights and all this stuff. Wow. Oh, should we bow?
cues.zh: 抱歉各位，我手里拿着相机呢。嗨，欢迎 Jimmy Long。很高兴认识你。我是 Tim。Tim，很高兴认识你。嘿，Mike。嘿。哇，你戴上手套了。这台庞然大物就在这儿。好的，稍后我们会正式介绍。我还带了灯光和所有这些设备。哇。噢，我们是不是得拜一拜？

cues.en: This is the holy computer. And Pat and Pat, I'll do that later. We should check if the analyzer made it alive, hopefully. Sure, probably do it off camera in case there's a big catastrophe.
cues.zh: 这可是神级计算机。还有 Pat 和 Pat，我待会儿再拍。我们得检查一下分析仪是不是还完好无损，希望一切正常。当然，最好在镜头外测，免得出什么大乱子。

cues.en: So it looks like I have just stepped into a hotel room full of nerds, my favorite kind of hotel rooms. And we all came here mostly because of this thing. So Mike, tell us what this is that I'm looking at. So this is an Apollo guidance computer.
cues.zh: 看来我刚走进了一间满是极客的旅馆房间，这正是我最喜欢的房间氛围。我们聚到这里，主要都是为了这个家伙。那么 Mike，告诉我们眼前这台到底是什么。这是一台阿波罗制导计算机。

cues.en: This is one of the original 15 computers built. This particular one came out of the first man-rated lunar module, the TA-8. Yeah, and by the way, Mike, sorry to interrupt, but... Mike is known because he has made an emulator of the AGC fully functional and gate exact. And now gets to work on the real thing because over here...
cues.zh: 这是最初制造的 15 台计算机之一。具体来说，这一台出自首个载人认证的登月舱，LTA-8。是的，顺便说一句，Mike，抱歉打断一下……Mike 很有名，因为他曾做过一个功能完全、门级精确的 AGC 仿真器。而现在他能接触真家伙了，因为在另一边……

cues.en: I'm going to turn to Jimmy. Jimmy over there. Hi Jimmy. Hi there. Jimmy is the owner. And tell us a little bit about this computer of yours where you worked at NASA, right? I worked for a short time on the test of the lunar excursion module, LTA-8. We actually man rated the limb for the first time.
cues.zh: 我把镜头转向 Jimmy。那边的 Jimmy。嗨，Jimmy。嗨，你好。Jimmy 是它的主人。能和我们讲讲你的这台计算机吗，你以前在 NASA 工作过，对吧？我曾短暂参与过登月舱 LTA-8 的测试工作。我们实际上是首次完成了登月舱的载人认证。

cues.en: In other words, we simulated a mission to the moon where we actually had the astronauts in the spacecraft. In 1976, I walked into a warehouse looking for some electronic components and I started seeing all this equipment that I recognized as being Apollo. So, I wound up buying two tons of Apollo out of that warehouse.
cues.zh: 换句话说，我们模拟了一次登月任务，宇航员真真切切地坐在飞船里面。1976 年，我走进一家仓库想找点电子元器件，结果看到的所有这些设备，我都认出属于阿波罗项目。所以，我最后从那个仓库里买下了整整两吨的阿波罗设备。

cues.en: My AGC was part of it. So that was in the two tons. And you just told me at dinner that this was actually the AGC in the lab that you were working on. Yes. And of course you were working in Houston. And you preserved all that, right? The two tons of it. I had two tons of it and for a long time I had no idea what I had.
cues.zh: 我的这台 AGC 就在其中。它就在那两吨设备里。你刚才吃晚饭时告诉我，这其实就是当年你在实验室工作时用的那台 AGC。是的。你当时当然是在休斯敦工作。而你把这些全都保存了下来，对吧？整整两吨。我留了整整两吨的设备，而且很长一段时间里，我都不知道自己手里到底有什么宝贝。

cues.en: I knew that it was from NASA, I knew it was Apollo, but I was not really that familiar with some of the items, and it took quite a bit of research to figure out what these items were. I think it was 2004, I actually met with the lead designer of the ABC, Mr. Eldon Hall, and we opened it up for the first time.
cues.zh: 我知道它来自NASA，知道它是Apollo，但我对其中有些部件并不太熟悉，花了不少研究才弄明白这些部件是什么。我想是2004年，我见到了ABC的首席设计师Eldon Hall先生，我们第一次把它打开。

cues.en: and found out that it was unpotted, which makes it pretty unique. Normally your AGCs are potted. In other words, you won't really see much of anything except for these black modules. With my AGC being unpotted, you can see all the beautiful integrated circuits and the wiring and everything. Here is one of the modules.
cues.zh: 结果发现它没有灌封，这相当独特。通常AGC都是灌封的。换句话说，除了这些黑色模块，你基本什么都看不到。我的AGC没有灌封，所以你能看到所有漂亮的集成电路、布线等等。这里是一个模块。

cues.en: Before I go to the modules, I go back to the picture of the AGC itself. So here it's two halves, and they are all made with this module. Maybe you can remove one. Sure. Maybe the memory or something that was easy to use. So we'll pull out one of these power supplies. These are the analog modules, right? Yeah. So this is the 4 volt power supply. It takes 28 volts in and it puts 4 volts out.
cues.zh: 在讲模块之前，我先回到AGC本身的照片。这里它是两半，而且全是用这种模块做的。也许你可以拆下一个。可以。也许内存或其他容易取用的东西。那我们就拔出一个电源。这些是模拟模块，对吧？对。这是4伏电源。它输入28伏，输出4伏。

cues.en: So the nice thing is that it's all written on it. But for something that was made in a hurry, it certainly doesn't look like it was made in a hurry. Kyle is grabbing another one. Careful there. So here's a more typical module. So this is a... Oh, that looks like a block one thing. Yeah, so this is a sense amplifier module. So there's 16 sense amplifier chips in here.
cues.zh: 好处是全都写在上面了。但对于一个赶工做出来的东西，它看起来可一点都不像赶工的。Kyle正在拿另一个。小心点。这是一个更典型的模块。这是一个……哦，那看起来像一整块的东西。对，这是一个读出放大器模块。这里面有16个读出放大器芯片。

cues.en: It's frequently said that there was only one type of integrated circuit in the AGC, but there were actually two. These sense amplifiers are another custom integrated circuit that they had made. So the red things down here are two-to-one transformers coming in from the core memories, and then the sense amplifiers pick that up, turn it into ones and zeros. And when Jimmy said they were unpotted, is that here is a... That's actually the module that this thing is famous for, because it has ICs in it.
cues.zh: 人们常说AGC里只有一种集成电路，但实际上有两种。这些读出放大器是他们另做的一种定制集成电路。下面这些红色的东西是来自核心存储器的2:1变压器，然后读出放大器接收信号，把它变成1和0。Jimmy说它们未灌封时，这里是一个……这其实就是这个模块出名的地方，因为它里面有IC。

cues.en: And we can see the ICs. Normally, it would be filled up with foam. Right. Then we couldn't access it. But since this one was a development LEM, they didn't pot it. Which means... Easy to test and repair. Right. They didn't check the signals on the chip. Exactly. So that was the explanation for the unpotted. At least getting a potted one out, right? Yep. Well, there are some that are potted. Yep. Just a few.
cues.zh: 我们可以看到这些IC。通常它会灌满泡沫。对。那样我们就接触不到它了。但既然这个是开发用的LEM，他们就没给它灌封。也就是说……便于测试和维修。对。他们没检查芯片上的信号。正是。所以这就是未灌封的解释。至少能把一个灌封的取出来，对吧？对。嗯，有些是灌封的。对。只有少数。

cues.en: There's the erasable memory, the current switch module, and the oscillator. So just to show... Oh, the erasable memory is plotted. Yes. Uh-oh. So if there is a fault in it... Yes, there is. And there is a fault in it. We are in trouble. Looks black. It's black, yeah. We can't really see what's going on in here. So luckily, this is one of only a few in here that are plotted.
cues.zh: 有可擦存储器、电流开关模块和振荡器。所以只是为了展示……哦，可擦存储器是灌封的。是的。哎呀。那么如果它里面出故障……是的，有故障。而且它确实有故障。我们就麻烦了。看起来是黑的。是黑的，对。我们其实看不到里面发生了什么。幸运的是，这是这里少数几个灌封的之一。

cues.en: Do we know if that one works? Not yet. But this one only has magnetic cores and transistors in it. Is it a read module for the memory? Or driver for the memory? And we actually have the schematics of that thing. Can you show a few pages, Kyle? So one of these pages is typically a single board. One of these modules has two boards, one on each side. So two pages of schematics.
cues.zh: 我们知道那个能用吗？目前还不知道。但这个里面只有磁芯和晶体管。它是内存的读取模块吗？还是内存的驱动模块？我们其实有那东西的原理图。Kyle，你能展示几页吗？通常这里的一页就对应一块板子。这种模块内部有两块板，正反各一块。所以对应两页原理图。

cues.en: one of these sliding modules. And how did we get to find the schematics? So Eldon Hall, the lead designer of the computer, had the schematics for all of the logic modules. And he made them available for scanning a bit over 10 years ago, I want to say, is when they became available. And then just more recently, Don Iles, who wrote
cues.zh: 这种抽拉式模块之一。那我们是怎么找到原理图的呢？是这样，这台计算机的首席设计师 Eldon Hall，留有所有逻辑模块的原理图。大概十多年前，他把这些图纸公开拿去扫描了，差不多就是那时候公开的。而就在最近，写了

cues.en: almost all of the landing code for the lunar module sent us a binder filled with schematics for all the logic modules and all of the rest of it, all the stuff that has been missing for the past 10 years. So he sent you? Yes, yes. So he mailed me this binder. So the story is actually you wanted to build a replica that was exact.
cues.zh: 登月舱几乎所有着陆代码的 Don Iles，寄给了我们一个活页夹，里面塞满了所有逻辑模块和其余所有部件的原理图，全是过去 10 年里一直缺失的内容。所以是他寄给你的？是的，没错。他把这个活页夹邮寄给了我。所以背后的故事其实是你想做个一模一样的复制品。

cues.en: and therefore you got to know everybody in it and you were after the schematics and eventually you found somebody ahead that was one of the original guys. Yes. And wow, that's a good find. Yeah. And so today we can follow the schematics and see if the gate work. Do they work?
cues.zh: 因此你认识了相关的每一个人，到处搜寻原理图，最后在当年元老级人物手里找到了。没错。哇，真是个了不起的发现。是的。所以今天我们能对照原理图，看看门电路能不能正常工作。它们能用吗？

cues.en: So far we have a hundred percent success rate with the three modules with all of the gates all of the chips in them We'd have one chip that malfunctioned initially but we realized from the failure that it was probably a metal was inside the chip a Manufacturing defect and by shaking it we dislodged it and the chip works fine now So your repair was to shake it was to shake it. Yep, and so therefore you can fly it again
cues.zh: 到目前为止，这三个模块里的所有门电路、所有芯片，成功率达到了 100%。最初有一颗芯片出了故障，但我们根据故障表现意识到，芯片内部可能有块金属杂质，属于制造缺陷，我们通过晃动把它弄出来了，现在芯片工作得很正常。所以你的维修手段就是晃晃它？就是晃晃它。对，所以它又能飞了。

cues.en: This is not flight-qualified anymore. Actually, we found that some of these gates are flight-qualified. Different modules have different sets of NOR gates in them. Oh, and you can tell which one is flight-qualified. Yeah, the flight-qualified ones have a red dot in the top left corner. Means they're tested to that highest level again. Ah, wow. Cool. And Mr. Ken has been hard at work also. I've been the only one goofing off.
cues.zh: 这已经不符合飞行认证标准了。其实我们发现其中一些门电路是符合飞行认证的。不同模块里装有不同的或非门组合。噢，你能看出来哪个符合飞行认证？是的，符合飞行认证的在左上角有个红点。代表它们再次通过了那种最高级别的测试。啊，哇。太酷了。Ken 先生也一直在埋头苦干。只有我一个人在摸鱼。

cues.en: and just filming things. Well, it just arrived, so I couldn't do anything else. What are you working on, Ken? So these are core rope simulators that you can plug in in place of the core rope, which we don't have, then connect to an external computer to simulate programs. Explain core ropes. Core rope, right? So to start the program for the Apollo guidance computer, it uses a special form of read-on memory called core rope, where they've wired
cues.zh: 只顾着四处拍摄。好吧，它刚送达，我也干不了别的。Ken，你在忙什么呢？这些是磁绳模拟器，你可以插上它来代替磁绳内存——反正在我们没有——然后连接到外部计算机来模拟程序。解释一下磁绳内存吧。磁绳，对吧？运行 Apollo 制导计算机的程序，需要使用一种特殊的只读存储器，叫做磁绳存储器，他们把导线

cues.en: wires through these cores to make the ones and the zeros. So the program is actually physically wired into this massive cores. So that's what we would call ROM today. That was the firmware, right? Yes, that's the program in ROM. This was used for ground testing. So instead of core rope, they would use these core rope simulators that let you feed in your test program from an external computer. It would go through the simulator into the pole guidance computer.
cues.zh: 穿过这些磁芯，来编出 1 和 0。所以程序实际上是用物理连线编进这堆庞大的磁芯里的。也就是我们今天所说的 ROM。那就是固件，对吧？没错，就是 ROM 里的程序。这是用于地面测试的。所以他们不使用磁绳，而是用这些磁绳模拟器，方便你从外部计算机输入测试程序。程序会通过模拟器输入到 Apollo 制导计算机中。

cues.en: And you can run whatever you want. So that box that you hold, that was in the AGC itself, it goes into the frame. Right, so this plugs in instead of the core rope modules. So this is the same size as the core modules.
cues.zh: 你可以运行任何程序。你手里拿的那个盒子原本就在 AGC 里，它会装进框架。对，所以它插上去替代核心绳模块。它和核心模块尺寸一样。

cues.en: Unfortunately, we don't have any documentation for this, so I'm trying to figure it out. Oh, that's not going to stop you? It's not going to well. Really? I can't imagine that. So it has this cordwood construction. Let me zoom on. Yes. It has this cordwood construction where they've mounted components vertically in a block of metal, so we can't see what they are or what they're doing. So it's very hard to know if is it a capacitor in here? Is it a transformer? Is it a transistor? We just have to kind of...
cues.zh: 不幸的是，我们没有任何相关文档，所以我正试着弄明白。哦，这不会拦住你吧？不会顺利的。真的？我无法想象。它有这种绳木式结构。让我放大看看。是的。它采用绳木式结构，元件垂直安装在金属块里，所以看不到它们是什么、在做什么。所以很难判断这里面是电容吗？是变压器吗？是晶体管吗？我们只能靠……

cues.en: you know, guess and figure it out. And we have no schematics or anything? Correct. Great. The other interesting thing is these modules here are used to hold integrated circuits. It's this bizarre technology that they used in the early 70s for prototyping integrated circuits that immediately fell into favor, but we're still stuck with this. Plus the problem is that the metal inside these is corroding and falling apart into little bits.
cues.zh: 你知道，靠猜来搞明白。而且我们没有任何原理图之类的东西？没错。太好了。另一个有趣的点是，这些模块用来固定集成电路。这是他们在 70 年代初用于集成电路原型验证的奇怪技术，很快受到青睐，但我们仍被它困住。还有个问题是，里面的金属正在腐蚀，碎成小片。

cues.en: So we have all these little bits of metal that we're finding inside with the integrated circuits. So we have to pull out all these bits of metal before they short something out. And they're metal from where? Let me show you. So these are called dipsticks. Do you have this food driver? Oh, they are part of a connector? You would think so, but... No. What's the second one?
cues.zh: 所以我们在集成电路附近发现了所有这些小金属碎屑。我们得在它们造成短路之前把所有金属碎屑弄出来。这些金属是哪来的？我给你看。这些叫 dipstick。你有这个 food driver 吗？哦，它们是连接器的一部分？你会这么想，但……不是。第二个是什么？

cues.en: So is this another core rope module? You have to use the two of them together. Oh okay. Because they're six core rope modules, so three per box. So let me open up one of the dipsticks and you can see what's going on. You should ask that on camera. I'm drinking from a fire hose here. So wait and look at what's inside. So inside the dipstick they have five integrated circuits mounted on this little clip and then you stick the clip into this.
cues.zh: 这是另一个核心绳模块吗？你得把两个一起用。哦好的。因为有六个核心绳模块，所以每个盒子三个。那让我打开一个 dipstick，你就能看到怎么回事。你该在镜头前问那个。我这儿信息量太大了。等等，看看里面。dipstick 里面有五块集成电路装在这个小夹子上，然后把这个夹子插进这个……

cues.en: This matching clip, and the pins are pinched between these. And on the other side, there's wire-wrapped pins where it's all connected. And there's supposed to be a metal bar that goes on top to hold these chips in place, but the metal bar has been falling apart into little bits of metal debris. That's the one that's disintegrated. And so you can see the metal bar stuck at the bottom here. Ouch. And because the metal bar is stuck, these three chips fell off the rail here.
cues.zh: 这个配套夹子，引脚被夹在两者之间。另一边是绕线引脚，全都连在一起。按理说上面应该有一根金属条把这些芯片固定住，但金属条一直在碎成小块金属碎屑。就是那根已经解体了。所以你能看到金属条卡在底部这里。哎哟。因为金属条卡住了，这三块芯片从导轨上掉下来了。

cues.en: There's chips. There you go. Stuck at the bottom. So your core module emulator is probably not working at this point. Well, it'll work. It just means the chips are stuck down there instead of here. Oh, they're still making contact. But when you put it together, they will still make contact. Here you can see the underside of the dipstick where each one of these is a pin of the IC on the inside. And then you can wire wrap your connections.
cues.zh: 有芯片。你看。卡在底部了。所以你的核心模块模拟器现在可能不工作。嗯，它会工作的。只是意味着芯片卡在那下面而不是这里。哦，它们仍然接触着。但当你把它装起来时，它们仍会接触。这里你能看到 dipstick 的底面，其中每一个都是内部 IC 的一个引脚。然后你就可以绕线连接了。

cues.en: Well, that's not a bad, it's a clean prototyping technique. Cleanly except for the metal debris and parts falling out and so forth. And being picky. And then on the top here they can put some decoupling capacitors. That makes for something that's prototype but very compact. And then over to the side, we will need a demo later on, but that's...
cues.zh: 这方法挺不错的，做原型很干净利落。要不是有那些金属碎屑和掉出来的零件的话。我吹毛求疵了。然后在顶上这里，可以放一些去耦电容。这样既保留了原型特性，又非常紧凑。然后旁边这边，我们待会儿需要演示一下，不过那是……

cues.en: Carl's handiwork. You can recognize it right away. Time pressure. Time pressure. But this is a diskie. To build it. A diskie built in a week. So obviously, Carl was going for functionality because we absolutely wanted... Oh! We of course wanted, if we had the time, if we were able to hook it up to the AGC.
cues.zh: Carl 的手艺。一眼就能认出来。时间紧迫。时间紧迫啊。但这可是一台 DSKY。为了把它造出来。一周内造出的一台 DSKY。显然，Carl 追求的是实用，因为我们非常想要……噢！如果我们有时间，我们当然想把它连到 AGC 上。

cues.en: The Miracles case where we can power it up. It's designed for the 28 volt logic levels of the AGC, so all those boards around the outside are the interfaces that are exact matches to the impedance of the design of the AGC. We expect no less from you, Carl. Exactly. So it's just... that's what your red boards and green boards are doing? Green boards are doing it. The red boards all the way to your left.
